claims.claim: Maqoma, son of Ngqika, born circa 1798; regent during Sandile's minority, 1829–1840.
Settlement near Kat River in 1822, forced removal 1829 and again 1833; land central to conflict.
Resistance in 1834–35 and Waterkloof campaign 1850–53; peace negotiations 1853.
Dispossession and warfare affected communities. Maqoma's role in cattle killing is disputed in consulted sources.
claims.uncertainty: Amathole says participated; SAHO biography says evidence suggests covert opposition. No single position assigned to him in narrative; no prophecy reenacted.

claims.claim: First imprisonment 1857/58; Katyi also on island; release 1869 and attempted resettlement.
claims.uncertainty: 1857 sentence/exile in Amathole vs 1858 arrival in museum timeline. Do not silently reconcile. Sentence length omitted. Individual daily activities and boat journeys illustrated symbolically, not documented episodes.

claims.claim: Reimprisoned 1871 without wife; died on Robben Island 9 September 1873. History preserved in research, museums and oral accounts.
claims.uncertainty: Cause and exact circumstances of death not established by this project. No deathbed scene or invented final words. No claim that present-day communities share a single interpretation.

visualPolicy: All images are new AI-assisted historical interpretations, not archival evidence. Faces, staging, weather and incidental people are reconstructions. No named dialogue, rituals, restricted knowledge or detailed genealogies invented. Plain clothing is a conservative artistic choice, not verified costume documentation. All artwork remains draft pending creator approval.
languagePolicy: Original AI-assisted isiXhosa draft, not a validated translation. No direct quotations. Fluent-speaker review must check grammar, terminology, names, readability and historical meaning before publication. Public credit selections do not imply permission verification.
